messages:
sam: heads up, customers flagged that the requests-per-minute metric on console is down ~40% starting after yesterday's sdk releases. anyone digging?

leila: saw the alert. console ingest shows fewer sampled traces; but raw request logs still match traffic. Looks like client-side sampling changed.

arjun: quick summary from SDK side: we shipped an internal perf helper in python/ts that toggles client sampling to reduce telemetry bandwidth. header set is `X-Obs-Sample: p=0.2`. intention was to default to p=1 for prod installs but helper accidentally flipped default to 0.2 for >=0.10.0.

marta: oof. So console dashboards are using sampled telemetry to backfill RPM and QPS tiles? That would undercount then.

leila: yes. current pipeline combines sampled spans with estimator logic. estimator assumes sampling rate is encoded in header `X-Obs-Sample` as a decimal fraction. But SDKs started encoding it as percentage string `20%` in some builds. Parser sees non-float and falls back to 1.0 -> but we also dropped sending the header when p==1 due to helper, so estimator sees no header and applies a 0.1 default. TL;DR: two bugs -> wrong default + wrong formatting.

sam: can you paste examples?

arjun: example payloads:

```
# old expected
X-Obs-Sample: 0.8

# broken (percent string)
X-Obs-Sample: 20%

# missing (helper omitted when 1.0 thought-unnecessary)
<no header>
```

marta: consequence: dashboard QPS undercount ~40% and some alerts fired (high perceived error rate because ratio metrics use sampled denominator). Not billing-impacting but huge customer confusion.

leila: recommended immediate actions: 1) push console parsing tolerant fix to interpret percentage strings and absence as 1.0 if we can confirm traffic; 2) patch SDKs to restore numeric float header default to 1.0 and stop omitting header; 3) create a temporary estimator override in console to use raw logs to rescale tiles for last 48h so customers see accurate trends.

arjun: SDK patch ready (branch: fix/obs-sample-format). We'll cut python 0.10.1 and ts 0.10.1 within the hour reverting helper behavior.

sam: can console do the tolerant parse fast? that seems lowest-risk.

leila: yes I'll open a PR to parse floats, percent-strings, and fallback policies: if header missing and request has a tracing span id, assume 1.0. If neither, mark as unknown and surface in tile. Owner: leila.

marta: I'll own the estimator override. Plan: for rolling window 48h, compute scale factor = raw-log-count / sampled-estimate and apply to QPS/RPM tiles only. Warn in dashboard that values are backfilled/adjusted.

telemetry-bot: new incident created: INC-2026-09-14-obs-sample-regression (severity: low)

arjun: publishing note: we should include migration text in changelog and fix the helper so it's opt-in via env var TELEMETRY_SAMPLING_HELPER=true. Also add a unit test for header formatting.

sam: good. timeline: console parsing patch -> canary in prod-2 in 30m. SDK patches published in next 60m. estimator backfill in 6h once we confirm new telemetry.

leila: canary deploy scheduled. I'll post PR link in this thread when opened.

arjun: python/ts releases queued. CI flakes on windows fixed in branch too.

marta: I'll coordinate a short customer note to explain the dashboard wobble and that quota/billing unaffected. Sam can review wording.

sam: will review. Also add an alert threshold to detect when sampled header fraction deviates >5% from expected baseline. Owner: sam.

telemetry-bot: deploy started: canary/obs-sample-tolerant-parser -> prod-2 (sha: d4e5f6)

leila: parser PR merged, canary running.

arjun: SDKs published (python 0.10.1, ts 0.10.1). npm/pypi shows successful publish.

marta: estimator backfill ran w/ scale factor 1.47 for last 48h. Dashboard tile updated and notice banner added.

sam: thanks everyone. owners recap: leila (parser + canary), arjun (sdk patch + publish), marta (estimator backfill + customer note), sam (alerts + signoff). checklist on the ticket. Closing in 12h unless new anomalies. :thumbsup:
